dashboard.subtitle: Overview of your platform

dashboard.shopClosedBody_other: <total></total> courses in the database, <published></published> published. A visitor cannot buy anything.
dashboard.datedNote: Every tile carries the date it was read. A tile without a date reads “not measured”, never an estimate.
dashboard.queueEmptyBody: No queue had a pending item at the last reading. Refresh to measure again.
dashboard.scope: This screen answers one question: what is blocking today. It carries no audience, no cohorts and no curves — analysis lives on /admin/analytics. Running costs — infrastructure, model calls, payment fees — are measured nowhere in the application, and revenue does not appear here: it is read on the Transactions screen. Queues are counted at the reading shown, not live.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.subtitle: Real platform statistics
analytics.popupsSubtitle: Last two months — exposed group and control group
analytics.popupsEmpty: No data yet. Counters are written by the Worker: they will only appear once `popupEvent` is deployed, and then from the first pop-up shown.
analytics.popupsNote: Click rate tells you how many visitors click, never whether the pop-up helped: a heavily clicked window can drive away more people than it converts. The "Control" column counts visitors who would have seen this pop-up but did not. Compare their conversions in GA4 — that comparison, and only that one, settles it.
analytics.advancedNote: For advanced traffic analytics (page views, sources, duration), integrate Google Analytics 4 or Plausible.
analytics.queueEmptyBody: No unhandled message, no unqualified lead, no overdue draft as of the last measurement.
analytics.scope: This screen measures; it steers nothing. It knows no audience, no traffic source, no visit duration, no cohort: those numbers are written nowhere in the database, and the “Devices” block that claimed to give them showed three values hard-coded in the file — it was removed rather than re-dated, because the rule does not say “date your estimates”, it says “never an estimate”. Pop-up counters are written by the Worker: a pop-up never shown has no row, and a missing row does not mean zero. Agency amounts are read from lead records, not from money received — a weighted pipeline is not revenue. And nothing is kept over time: each measurement overwrites the previous one, there is no series.

appointments.title: Appointments
appointments.emptyBody: The tiles count the whole collection; the stage and the search only filter the display.
appointments.scope: Confirming or cancelling writes a status to the database and sends nothing: no e-mail, no SMS, no calendar invite. The person who asked for the slot will only know your answer if you write to them yourself, and no calendar is kept up to date anywhere else. The slot is not checked either: two requests can be confirmed on the same hour. The kit files this screen under “upcoming / past”; the pattern forbids filtering by date, so the stage stays the status.

agencyLeads.title: Agency leads
agencyLeads.notesPlaceholder: Context, budget mentioned, objection, next follow-up...
agencyLeads.notesHint: Saved automatically when you leave the field. Never visible to the lead.
agencyLeads.emptyBody: The tiles count the whole collection; the stage and the search only filter the display.
agencyLeads.scope: No automatic follow-up: every chase is a manual gesture, and nothing reminds you of a forgotten lead. The kit plans two sales cycles side by side — Présence Digitale and Max-Morrys Agency; the database stores only one, `agency_leads`, fed by /presence-digitale, so the second is not displayed. The monthly plan has no direct-debit rail in Senegal: a contract signed here is not revenue collected, and no amount on this screen ever reaches Transactions.

This screen shows neither enrolments, nor progress, nor certificates for a course — they live elsewhere in the console. And it does not order courses: the public catalogue sorts by creation date, not from here.

coupons.scope: This screen refuses nothing: the payment server alone turns down a stopped, expired or used-up coupon. Nor does it say what a discount cost — reconciliation with payments happens in Transactions. A coupon switched off by hand has no stage of its own: it only shows under “all”.

announcements.title: Announcements
announcements.empty: No announcements. Create the first one.
announcements.emptyBody: The banner only shows when an announcement is active AND inside its date window.
announcements.linkHint: Internal path or full URL. The banner opens it in the visitor's language.
announcements.scope: This screen administers the public site banner: a title, a date window, a link. It measures nothing — no impression, no click, no dismissal — and the banner has no control group, so no rate can be shown here. The control group the kit names belongs to the contextual pop-ups, which are a different mechanism: their exposed share of traffic is set in Settings, and their counters — exposed against control — are read in Analytics. Finally, an announcement outside its window stays “active” in the database; it is simply not served.

faq.title: FAQ

form.slugHint: Left empty, it's derived from the question — and moves if you reword it. Filled in, it's fixed.

faq.emptyBody: A question asked three times in writing is worth an entry here — that is three fewer messages.
faq.scope: A question has no draft: it goes live the moment it's saved, and its order is typed by hand. Every question now has its own page — /faq/<address> — with its trail, its nearby questions and its structured data. The « derived slug » stage counts the ones whose address is NOT fixed: it's derived from the text, so rewording the question moves the page and breaks links already shared, with nothing to signal it. This screen still doesn't say which questions get read or which ones are missing: nothing is measured on /faq.

messages.title: Messages

confirm.deleteMessage: Delete this message? This action is irreversible.

messages.scope: No reply leaves this screen: “Reply by email” opens the device's mail client, and nothing written there comes back to the record. “Closed” therefore does not mean a reply went out — it means someone said so. No thread, no attachment, no follow-up, and no screen on the visitor's side: whoever wrote will only learn where their message stands by receiving an answer.

console.scope: “Imported” is a PROVENANCE, not a status: a hand-written draft therefore has no stage of its own and shows only under “all”. The import never updates an episode already pulled in — it only creates the missing ones. And nothing goes back out to Spotify: the flow is one-way, and no notification announces an episode.

console.scope: The view count only moves when the sync runs: in between, it is stale. This screen publishes nothing to YouTube and reads neither comments, nor watch time, nor subscriptions. No video is hosted here: deleting a record leaves the video online on YouTube.

testimonials.title: Testimonials
testimonials.scope: This screen moderates; it collects nothing. No identity check, no recorded consent, no collection date: a testimonial is worth exactly what the person who typed it is worth. “Approve” features it, and the Club subscription page then shows it as social proof — this is the only screen that puts it there, and the only one that can take it back. The import button writes six demo testimonials, signed with people's names, into that same collection: nothing tells them apart afterwards. Star ratings are no longer drawn here; the field stays in the database.

transactions.title: Transactions
transactions.refundExplainBody: The button writes the “refunded” status onto the transaction, and nothing else. No money moves as a result: the refund happens at the payment provider, and this screen only records it afterwards. The enrolment already granted is not withdrawn.
transactions.emptyBody: The tiles above count the whole table; the stage and the search only filter the display.
transactions.scope: This screen only RECONCILES: it reads what the payment webhook wrote and has no way to replay it, nor to force an enrolment that a completed transaction failed to trigger. No refund starts here — it happens at the provider, and the button only records the trace. On the buyer side there is no history screen at all: anyone wanting to know where their payment stands has to write in, and nobody will know before that.

settings.popupTreatmentDesc: The rest forms the control group, which sees no pop-ups at all. That is what tells you whether they genuinely help, not merely whether they get clicked. At 100% there is no control group and no comparison left.
settings.popupsCacheNote: At most one pop-up per session, and seven days before the same one is offered again. Settings are cached for the visitor's session: turning one off takes effect on their next visit.
settings.toastSaveError: Error while saving. Please try again.
settings.securityReadOnlyNote: These three lines are written in the screen’s own code: they describe the expected configuration, they do not query it.
settings.scope: Neither payment, nor search, nor roles are configured here. The payment provider's keys live in Cloud Functions secrets; redirects and the sitemap are produced elsewhere — the “Redirects” screen and the Worker's prerender; an account's role is changed under “Users”. Saving writes a single Firestore document straight from the browser: the operation is not logged, and nothing will later say who switched off which pop-up, or when. Pop-up settings are cached for the length of a visitor's session — switching one off only becomes visible on their next visit.

users.title: Users
users.emptyBody: Change stage or clear the search: the four stages count the whole database, the search only filters what is left.
users.scope: No suspension here: the data model carries no “suspended” state, so the kit stage that shows it has no source and is not displayed. Cutting someone off happens in the Firebase console, and that gesture leaves no trace in the application. Deleting an account, resetting a password and revoking open sessions do not exist on this screen either.

missions.emptyBody: Requests arrive from the /agence form. Nothing to do while the queue is empty.
missions.notesDirty: Note not saved yet — it is written when the field loses focus.
missions.scope: No follow-up is automatic: every touch is a manual gesture, and nothing here writes to the prospect — the button opens their own mail client. The filter sorts the six statuses of the agency cycle into two queues; the precise status is chosen on the record. No conversion rate is shown: the one the data layer computes counts still-open requests as “decided”, so it measures nothing stable. And a won request is not money received — no collection rail runs through this screen.

redirects.emptyBody: An old URL with no redirect is a page lost to search engines.

conflictHints.duplicate: Two active entries share this source. The Worker keeps only one — the most recently updated — and the other never applies.
conflictHints.loop: The target is the source itself: the browser loops, then gives up, and the address becomes unreachable.
conflictHints.chain: The target is itself the source of another active redirect. Visitors take two hops, search engines discount the chain, and an A→B→A round trip loops. Point straight at the final destination.
conflictHints.unserved: The Worker drops this entry silently: a source reduced to “/”, or a target that is not an internal path, is never served.

redirects.scope: This screen writes the table; it does not try it. The Worker caches it for one minute, and the “in conflict” stage reads the table, never real traffic. Click counts exist for attribution links only: an SEO 301 is never counted, because bots follow most of them. And a redirect typed here does not replace the in-app hops: /podcasts and /videos currently reach /podcast-et-videos in JavaScript, which passes no ranking on — the two 301 entries are still to be typed in.
